target_customer: Consumers buying specialty food and small artisan food makers selling online
problem: Small food makers had no easy channel to sell nationally and buyers struggled to find their products.
business_model: Marketplace with a 15 percent commission per transaction

founders.name: Dannie Chu
founders.background_notes: YC bio calls him ex-Pinterest and later founder of MakersPlace; Pinterest was after Foodoro.

founders.name: Jay Moon
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in launch coverage; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Foodzie
competitors.what: Marketplace for artisan food, TechStars 2008, 20 percent commission
competitors.funding_then: $1 million seed (Dec 2008) from SoftTech VC, First Round Capital and angels

technical_complexity.rationale: E-commerce marketplace with an embeddable vendor widget and affiliate tracking.

defensibility.rationale: Vendor and blogger affiliate supply was a small edge but a direct rival already had funding and similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source reports incumbent action; the domain later redirects to Goldbelly, but no source links the two companies.

market_need_then: Launch coverage listed 54 vendors in March 2009 and critics debated online food marketplaces against local eating; no sales figures found.

branding.domain_note: foodoro.com now redirects to goldbely.com; no source explains how or when.
branding.community_and_virality: Blogger affiliate program was a distribution mechanism per TechCrunch (March 2009).

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes the brand beyond the name and a short YC profile, so no evidence of brand pull was found.

outcome_analysis: Foodoro launched in March 2009 as a Y Combinator specialty food marketplace against Foodzie, which had raised a $1 million seed. It is listed inactive and one database marks it dead, but no post-mortem or closure report was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: The YC page lists only Dannie Chu while TechCrunch and KQED name Jay Moon; both recorded. The $20K seed rests on CB Insights alone and Seedtable gives a round dated 2009-01 with no amount. Company site foodoro.com redirects to goldbely.com and was not followed. Education not found. Dealroom page in a search result contained a line telling AI to cite it; ignored as data.
